26:T433,On the remote plains of the Channel Country, in western Queensland, travelers of the Australian outback have recounted since the 19th century a light —the 'Min Min'— that appears at night, seems to follow whoever observes it, keeps its distance, and fades when approached. The name comes from a now-vanished hotel on the route between Boulia and Winton; the tradition is even older, present in Aboriginal accounts. In 2003, neuroscientist Jack Pettigrew (University of Queensland) proposed, from a number of direct observations and a field demonstration, that the Min Min light is a Fata Morgana-type mirage: light from real and very distant natural or man-made sources, ducted over tens or hundreds of kilometers by a thermal inversion of cold air over the ground. His paper concludes that these optics explain 'many of the strange properties' of the light 'if account is also taken of the human factors' of someone watching an isolated light with no landmarks; in his demonstration, the light of a car placed below the line of sight appeared floating above the ed:T461,On April 11, 1980, at La Joya Air Base (Arequipa, Peru), Peruvian Air Force lieutenant Óscar Santa María Huertas scrambled in a Sukhoi Su-22 fighter to intercept an object the base initially took for a spy balloon. He fired 64 of his 140 rounds in a first burst that, by his testimony, the object seemed to absorb without damage; on the following attempts the object moved away just as he locked onto it. The object —described as about 10 meters across, with a shiny cream-colored dome over a silver circular base, like a cut light bulb— withstood 22 minutes of pursuit, was seen by hundreds of people at the base, and remained stationary for about two more hours. The only contemporaneous document is a report from the U.S. defense attaché office in Lima, received in Washington on June 3, 1980, which dates the episode to May 9, records second-hand the firing 'at very close range without causing any apparent damage', adds a second sighting and a second Su-22 scramble on May 10, and concludes that 'its origin remains unknown'. Santa María is the only documented pilot to have fired at an unidentified 1d0:T4d2,In March 1952, Captain Edward J. Ruppelt — director of the Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) Project Blue Book at Wright-Patterson AFB — gave a 'flying saucer' lecture to scientists at MIT Lincoln Laboratory (a FFRDC founded in 1951 at Hanscom AFB, Massachusetts). The talk was captured on reel-to-reel tape and catalogued as 'AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52.' The recording remained in MIT Lincoln Lab's possession for 74 years. On June 24, 2026, Rep. Eric Burlison (R-MO) confirmed that MIT Lincoln Lab acknowledged the file's existence and agreed to hand it over to Congress. It is the first known recording of an official USAF briefing on UAP/flying saucers to civilian defense contractors, made four months before the 'Invasion of Washington' of July 1952. On 18 September 2026 the sixth PURSUE release published the audio of a March 1952 Ruppelt presentation together with its full transcript; the month, the speaker, the subject and the medium all match, but no document in the release names the laboratory. On 21 September Burlison's office stated in a press release that this was the recording he had sought, although the identification comes from the party that requested it, not from the laboratory or 1d1:T4b0,Document 341_110677 (PURSUE Release 01) contains Air Intelligence Information Report IR 193-55, signed on October 14, 1955 by U.S. air attaché Lt. Col. Thomas S. Ryan. It records the account of three 'highly reliable' U.S. observers who, traveling by rail through the Trans-Caucasus (between Aliaty and Adzhijabul, south of Baku) on October 4, 1955 at 19:10, saw two disc-shaped objects ascend almost vertically —with the outer surface revolving slowly to the right— to about 6,000 feet, at which point they sharply accelerated northward. The take-off area, 1-2 miles south of the line, showed two searchlight beams pointing almost vertically. The attaché assessed it as significant for the USAF's UFO project. The report's summary does not name them, but the attaché's cable to USAF headquarters of October 13, transcribed on page 2 of the same report, does identify those 'three observers', as the CIA memo CIA-UAP-D020 (PURSUE Release 04) later also does: Senator Richard Russell, then chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee; his military aide, the same Lt. Col. E. U. Hathaway cited as the report's source; and interpreter Ruben Efron. 76:"On the night of September 19-20, 1961, Betty and Barney Hill reported that a light followed their car in New Hampshire's White Mountains and, under hypnosis more than two years later with psychiatrist Benjamin Simon, recounted an abduction. Simon concluded that the abduction memories were a fantasy born of Betty's dreams."

(Harry) Turner, head of the Nuclear Branch of Australia's Joint Intelligence Organisation (JIO), and addressed to its Director through the Director of Scientific and Technical Intelligence. It attaches two studies: one on the official U.S. attitude to UFOs, compiled, by Turner's own account, from public reports and statements by the CIA, the USAF, Congressional hearings and Blue Book, and another on alleged 'weapon systems' drawn from Jacques Vallée's catalogue of landing reports. It argues that UFOs are real, that the CIA used the Robertson panel to debunk them and that the U.S. launched an anti-gravity program. It is one analyst's thesis, not an assessment adopted by JIO: the same day, Director R. W. Furlonger acknowledged that some reports could not readily be explained, but asked that no significant JIO resources be devoted to them. 1d6:T6cb,PURSUE (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters) is the executive directive signed by the Trump administration in May 2026 ordering the newly renamed Department of War (formerly DoD) to execute an 'expeditious' interagency release of unresolved UAP records. The war.gov/ufo/ portal opened on May 8, 2026 and published in successive tranches: Release 1 (May 8), Release 2 (May 22), Release 3 (June 12), Release 4 (July 10) and Release 5 (August 7). By mid-June the portal had surpassed 1.7 billion accesses. The AARO assessment accompanying the third release (signed by its director Jon Kosloski, June 5) emphasizes 'plasma-like' orbs —including an orange 'mother orb' releasing smaller red orbs— and concedes that ~40% of cases remain unexplained. The fourth release (July 10, 2026) contributed 40 additional files (14 documents, 19 videos, 4 audio recordings, 3 images), including infrared video of a six-pointed object over the Yellow Sea captured by U.S. Indo-Pacific Command in 2025, testimony from a military aviator with 28 years of service about a rectangular object with 'flight characteristics unlike anything I had seen' (Eastern US, 2019), documentation of an intrusion over the Pantex nuclear plant (Texas, September 2015), and a transcript of a Los Alamos conference (1949) where physicists attempted to explain the 'green fireballs' over the nuclear laboratory. It is the first U.S. federal UAP-release infrastructure with a direct presidential mandate and a stable public URL. The content remains more procedural than probative —orb videos, historical audio and declassified documents, without the conclusive piece that would settle the material question— but it is no longer
